claims.text: Rapidly quenched nominal FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure containing fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The FeCoNiTi system has ferromagnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
Coexistence of C14 with fcc FeCoNiTi can raise coercivity to approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The Ti-rich C14 sublattice couples antiferromagnetically to the Fe/Co/Ni-rich fcc matrix.
Antiferromagnetic coupling to C14 suppresses the saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
The fcc-C14 interfaces create strong magnetic anisotropy.
The fcc-C14 phase boundaries act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
Varying Ti content will modulate the volume fraction and morphology of the C14 phase.
Increasing fcc-C14 interfacial area will maximize the proposed antiferromagnetic coupling.
At 400 K, the fcc phase remains within its ferromagnetically ordered regime and below the relevant Curie temperature.
Hybridization between Ti 3d states in C14 and Fe/Co 3d states in fcc mediates interfacial magnetic pinning.
Lattice mismatch and chemical segregation at the interface generate high local magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than a single-phase fcc reference.
Coupling between the phases will measurably shift the magnetic transition temperatures.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments and the absence of phase-boundary pinning.
The proposed magnetic mechanism requires a continuous or semi-continuous reticulated C14 network rather than isolated C14 islands.
HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 contains BCC and Laves phases, with the Laves phase exhibiting a reticulated morphology.
The coercivity enhancement diminishes if C14 becomes nonmagnetic or interfacial chemical disorder magnetically decouples the phases.
Spin-polarized first-principles DFT should be used to calculate the spin density of states at the Fermi level, exchange splitting, and orbital moments of the fcc and C14 phases.
Temperature-dependent magnetization and hysteresis measurements on dual-phase, C14-dominant, and single-phase-fcc comparators can isolate phase-specific magnetic transitions and coercivity.

contradictions.description: Rapid quenching is said to produce the initial dual-phase fcc+C14 state, but it is also proposed as a means of suppressing C14 formation in the comparator without specifying a distinct quench rate or other processing difference.
The second alloy is described ambiguously as either C14-dominant or single-phase fcc, which are opposite phase conditions; the falsification rule subsequently treats it specifically as C14-dominant.

The mechanism attributes the high coercivity to interfacial anisotropy and domain-wall pinning despite an intrinsically limited fcc orbital moment, whereas the uncertainty statement refers to an orbital-moment enhancement as being required to reach 667 Oe.
